[kimi @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness, negation, agency, modality, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/6: [agency] "his fear of God restrained him" vs "φόβῳ τῷ πρὸς θεὸν ἐπέσχε τὸ ἀμύνασθαι": Subject is fear (φόβῳ), not 'his fear'; 'he restrained himself' misreads middle voice; [negation] "there is no other way...unless one is guarded" vs "οὐκ ἔστιν ἑτέρως ἀβλαβεῖς ἀπαλλάττεσθαι μὴ οὐχὶ φόβῳ θεοῦ φρουρουμένους": μὴ οὐχὶ = 'except by' not 'unless'; double negative construction flattened; [modality] "he has made this the goal" vs "πεποιῆσθαι σκοπόν": Infinitive πεποιῆσθαι (perfect passive/middle) not finite 'he has made'; dependent on ἔλεγε; [completeness] "For those from circumcision despise him, because" vs "ἐξευτελίζουσι γὰρ αὐτὸν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς ἀλήστῳ μνήμῃ φυλάττοντα": Participial phrase ἀλήστῳ μνήμῃ φυλάττοντα not causal 'because he keeps' but descriptive 'keeping' | part 2/6: [source_identity] "he awaited eternal salvation, and now also, longing for it, he has made this the goal of his study of the law" vs "ἀναζήσεσθαι γὰρ δὴ καὶ αἰνέσειν θεὸν λέγει": Invented clause 'goal of his study of the law' not in source; 'awaited eternal salvation' and 'longing for it' are unsupported additions.; [agency] "My soul will live" vs "Ζήσεται ἡ ψυχή μου": Changed person: Greek is third person 'will live,' not first person 'My soul will live' as if quoting; the psalmist's words are cited in third person.; [scripture] "Psalm 118:175 [119:175]" vs "Ps 119,2": Wrong verse reference: Greek has Ps 119:2 (LXX) = Ps 119:176 (Hebrew), not 119:175; the citation number is incorrect.; [negation] "He does not foresee the cessation that will come then" vs "οὐ προορᾷ τὴν παῦλαν ἐσομένην τότε": Wrong subject: the Greek says the afflicted person 'does not foresee,' but context suggests this is a statement about human limitation, not a specific individual's failure; however the negation itself is correct. More seriously: 'the cessation that will come then' implies future cessation is denied, but Greek says he does not foresee the cessation that will-be then—meaning he lacks foresight of it, not that it won't happen.; [completeness] "with good and bad alike sharing its citizenship" vs "τὴν σὺν ἀγαθοῖς καὶ κακοῖς πολιτείαν": Missing 'the' citizenship; more importantly, 'sharing its citizenship' adds 'sharing' not in Greek, which simply says 'the with good and bad citizenship'—the sense is citizenship alongside good and bad, not necessarily 'sharing' it. | part 3/6: [scripture] "Psalm 120:1b-2 [121:1b-2]" vs "Ps 120,1b®2": Greek cites Ps 120 LXX (=121 MT), but bracketed English should be [121:1b-2], not [121:1b-2]—actually this is correct. Wait: checking again: LXX 120 = MT 121, so [121:1b-2] is correct. No error.; [completeness] "Another passage also indicates the foreign land in one respect" vs "ἄλλος καὶ τὴν ἀλλόφυλον χώραν ἐξ ἑνὸς μέρους": Missing 'shows/declares' (δηλοῖ); 'indicates' is acceptable synonym. No error.; [agency] "his sojourning was extended" vs "παρατεῖναι τὴν παροικίαν αὐτοῦ": Passive 'was extended' obscures active infinitive 'to extend his sojourning'—but this is acceptable idiom. No error.; [completeness] "for this is the longest sojourning" vs "αὕτη γὰρ ἡ μακροτάτη": Missing 'sojourning' (παροικία), but implied from context. No error.; [completeness] "as far as depends on them" vs "τὸ ἐξ αὐτῶν": 'the [thing] from themselves' = 'as far as depends on them' is acceptable idiom. No error.; [negation] "would never enter into friendship with the good" vs "οὐδέ ποτ' ἂν ἀγαθοῖς εἰς φιλίαν συμβαῖεν": Correctly negated. No error.; [completeness] "anything good from the godly" vs "τὸ χρηστόν τι παρὰ τῶν θεοσεβῶν": Correct. No error.; [completeness] "nor are they tamed by their kindness" vs "οὐδὲ ἡμεροῦνται τῇ παρ' ἐκείνων φιλανθρωπίᾳ": 'their kindness' = 'the from-those benevolence'; acceptable. No error.; [completeness] "And while he awaits help through them" vs "καὶ τὴν βοήθειαν διὰ τούτων περιμένων": Missing 'says' (λέγει) for this clause—'he says' appears later. But 'awaiting' is participle, rendered as finite 'awaits' acceptable. No error. | part 4/6: [scripture] "Psalm 121:1b-4 [122:1b-4]" vs "Ps 121,1b®4": Greek cites Ps 121:1b-4 (LXX); English brackets [122:1b-4] correct but verse range '1b-4' mismatches Hebrew 122:2-5 or similar; [agency] "the ones who speak to the prophets" vs "τῶν λαλούντων προφήταις": Greek dative προφήταις means 'speaking to/among prophets' or 'speaking as prophets', not 'to the prophets' as recipients; [completeness] "interceding for fallen Jerusalem and speaking of her future dwelling" vs "πρεσβεύων τε ὑπὲρ τῆς πεπτωκυίας Ἱερουσαλὴμ καὶ τὴν μέλλουσαν αὐτῆς λέγων κατοίκησιν": Dropped τε 'both/and' linking two participles; 'speaking of' obscures λέγων 'saying' introducing direct speech; [agency] "The psalmist says that he rejoiced when he heard these things" vs "ὁ ὑμνῳδὸς ἀκηκοὼς ηὐφρᾶνθαί φησι": Greek has psalmist as subject of 'says', with 'having heard' and 'rejoiced' as participial/infinitival complements, not 'when he heard'; [completeness] "and, as it were, perceived the matter as present prophetically" vs "καὶ οἱονεὶ παρόντος τοῦ πράγματος αἰσθόμενος προφητικῶς": Dropped explicit 'of the thing being present' (genitive absolute); 'as present' compresses the syntax; [scripture] ""Our feet were standing in the courts of Jerusalem"" vs "Ἑστῶτες ἦσαν οἱ πόδες ἡμῶν ἐν ταῖς αὐλαῖς Ἱερουσαλήμ": Greek has 'Standing were the feet of-us', not 'Our feet were standing'; English inverts for naturalness but alters emphasis; [completeness] "The standing of feet is the immovable dwelling" vs "στάσις δὲ ποδῶν ἡ ἀμετακίνητός ἐστι κατοίκησις": Dropped δὲ 'but/and'; 'The standing of feet' nominalizes where Greek has 'standing but of-feet the immovable is dwelling'; [completeness] "The opposite of this was when, according to the history, God shook the foot of Jerusalem from its own land" vs "οὗ τοὐναντίον ἦν ὅτε κατὰ τὴν ἱστορίαν ἐσάλευσεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν πόδα Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἀπὸ γῆς τῆς οἰκείας": Dropped οὗ 'of which' linking back; 'the foot' singular πόδα not 'foot' as English has but 'foundation/base' or literal 'foot' | part 5/6: [completeness] "to give thanks to the name of the Lord" vs "τοῦ ἐξομολογήσασθαι τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου": ἐξομολογήσασθαι means 'to confess/praise' not 'to give thanks'; [completeness] "were thrown around them" vs "τείχη περιεβάλλοντο": middle voice: 'walls were thrown around' (impersonal), not 'around them' | part 6/6: [completeness] "It is a testimony to Israel" vs "μαρτύριον μὲν τῷ Ἰσραήλ": Dropped 'μὲν...δὲ' contrastive structure ('on the one hand...on the other hand'); [completeness] "and to give thanks to the name of the Lord" vs "τοῦ ἐξομολογήσασθαι δὲ τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου": Dropped 'δέ' ('on the other hand'); 'τοῦ' is genitive article, not 'and to'; [agency] "confession of grace is owed by the beneficiaries" vs "ἐξομολόγησις χαρίτων ὀφείλεται παρὰ τῶν εὐεργετουμένων": 'χαρίτων' is genitive plural 'of graces/favors', not 'of grace'; beneficiaries give thanks, not receive grace

ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. 'My soul will live' quotes the psalm's Ζήσεται ἡ ψυχή μου (Ps 118:175), which the Greek introduces as the following words (ἐπάγεται τὸ Ζήσεται ἡ ψυχή μου, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς), so the first person is correct and the reference [119:175] is right; 'Ps 119,2' is the next fragment's lemma. 'He has made this the goal of his study of the law' renders ταύτην πεποιῆσθαι σκοπὸν … τοῦ νόμου μελέτης, which is in the Greek. οὐ προορᾷ 'he does not foresee' is the Greek. 'Psalm 120:1b-2 [121:1b-2]' and '121:1b-4 [122:1b-4]' are correct LXX/English pairs. The rest (μέν/δέ, χαρίτων, 'give thanks' for ἐξομολογήσασθαι, participle syntax) is idiom.
